title: Assessment of Various Entities
outcomes: Apply company tax rates and concessional regimes.
Compute MAT and old MAT credit.
Assess firms, LLPs, AOPs and HUFs.
Apply tonnage tax and succession provisions.

meta.exam_tip: Compute tax on normal provisions first, then the minimum tax, and pay the higher.

concepts.title: Taxation of companies and concessional regimes
body: Domestic companies pay 25% where turnover in T.Y. 2024-25 did not exceed ₹400 crore and 30% otherwise; foreign companies pay 35%. Surcharge for domestic companies is 7% above ₹1 crore and 12% above ₹10 crore of income (2% and 5% for foreign companies), plus 4% cess.

Section 200 lets a domestic company opt for 22% plus a flat 10% surcharge, giving up specified exemptions and deductions; section 201 offers 15% to new manufacturing or electricity-generating companies meeting conditions. Once exercised, the option cannot be withdrawn and MAT does not apply.
Income of these companies from special sources (e.g. capital gains) is taxed at the rates applicable to them; deemed income under section 201 attracts 30%.
concepts.analogy: Choose between the regular rate with deductions and a flat concessional rate.
concepts.work: A company opting for section 200 pays an effective rate of about 25.17%.

concepts.title: Minimum alternate tax and MAT credit
body: Section 206(1): if tax on total income is lower than 14% of book profit (9% for IFSC units earning solely in convertible foreign exchange), book profit is deemed the total income and MAT is payable, plus surcharge and cess. Book profit starts from the net profit in the statement of profit and loss prepared under the Companies Act and is adjusted for specified items.

MAT does not apply to life insurance companies, companies opting for sections 200 or 201, and specified foreign companies without a permanent establishment or not required to register in India, or taxed only on presumptive income.

MAT credit carried forward on 31 March 2026 under section 115JAA: a domestic company that switches to section 200/201 can set off up to 25% of its tax payable each year (section 206(3)); a foreign company may use it to the extent normal tax exceeds MAT (section 206(4)); in both cases within 15 years from when the credit first arose. No credit passes to an LLP on conversion.
concepts.analogy: MAT ensures companies pay at least 14% of book profit.
concepts.work: Old credit of ₹8 lakh can absorb ₹3.15 lakh of a ₹12.58 lakh liability.

concepts.title: Alternate minimum tax for non-corporates
body: Section 206(2): non-corporate assessees claiming profit-linked deductions in Chapter VIII-C (other than co-operatives' section 149 deduction) or investment-linked deductions under section 46 pay AMT at 18.5% of adjusted total income (9% for IFSC units; 15% for co-operatives) if regular tax is lower.
Adjusted total income adds back these deductions (with depreciation substituted for section 46 deductions).

AMT does not apply to persons taxed under the default regime of section 202(1), to those opting for concessional co-operative regimes, or to individuals, HUFs, AOPs, BOIs and artificial juridical persons whose adjusted total income does not exceed ₹20 lakh.
concepts.analogy: Profit-linked deductions cannot drive tax below 18.5%.
concepts.work: An LLP start-up deducting all profits under section 140 still pays AMT.

concepts.title: Firms, LLPs, AOPs and HUFs
body: A firm or LLP is taxed at 30% (plus surcharge and cess); remuneration and interest to partners are deductible within section 35(e) limits and taxed in partners' hands, while the profit share is exempt. Partners of a firm are jointly and severally liable for its tax; partners of an LLP are liable on liquidation unless they prove no gross neglect (section 331).

AOPs and BOIs: if member shares are unknown, tax is at the maximum marginal rate (section 311). Section 309 computes each member's share after adjusting payments to members; under section 310, if the AOP paid at maximum marginal or higher rate, the share is excluded from the member's income.

HUFs: a Hindu undivided family continues to be assessed until a partition is recorded under section 315; partial partitions are ignored. Income from property converted into HUF property by a member is clubbed with him (section 99(3)).
concepts.analogy: Each entity type has its own rate and pass-through rules.
concepts.work: An AOP with unknown member shares pays tax at the maximum marginal rate.

concepts.title: Tonnage tax and succession
body: Tonnage tax (sections 225 to 234): an Indian shipping company may opt to have profits from qualifying ships computed on a notional basis linked to net tonnage, instead of actual profits. The option runs for 10 years and requires conditions such as training cadets and transferring a portion of profits to a reserve.

Section 313: where a business is succeeded, the predecessor is assessed up to the date of succession and the successor thereafter; the AO may recover tax from the successor if the predecessor cannot be found.
Section 323: directors of a private company are jointly and severally liable for its unrecoverable tax unless they prove non-recovery is not due to their gross neglect, misfeasance or breach of duty.
concepts.analogy: Special schemes and recovery rules apply to particular situations.
concepts.work: A shipowner can pay tax on notional tonnage income regardless of actual profits.

jobs.title: Regime decision for a company
jobs.situation: A listed company with MAT credit considers moving to section 200.
steps: Compute tax under normal provisions and MAT.
Recommend and file the option in time.
jobs.takeaway: Old MAT credit slows but rarely blocks the switch.

mcqs.q: MAT rate for a company outside IFSC is:
mcqs.explain: Section 206(1). In practice: plus surcharge and cess.
mcqs.topic: Minimum alternate tax and MAT credit

mcqs.q: MAT does not apply to a company that:
mcqs.explain: Concessional regime. In practice: irreversible option.
mcqs.topic: Minimum alternate tax and MAT credit

mcqs.q: Old MAT credit can be set off by a domestic company under section 200 up to:
mcqs.explain: Section 206(3). In practice: balance carried forward.
mcqs.topic: Minimum alternate tax and MAT credit

mcqs.q: AMT rate for a non-corporate assessee (non-IFSC, non-co-operative) is:
mcqs.explain: Section 206(2). In practice: on adjusted total income.

mcqs.q: AMT does not apply to an individual whose adjusted total income does not exceed:
mcqs.explain: Threshold for individuals and similar persons. In practice: also not in default regime.

mcqs.q: An AOP whose members' shares are unknown pays tax at:
mcqs.explain: Section 311. In practice: draft clear deeds.

mcqs.q: Section 200 rate for domestic companies is:
options: Twenty-two percent plus ten percent surcharge
mcqs.explain: Concessional option. In practice: forgo deductions.

mcqs.q: Directors of a private company are liable for unrecovered tax unless they prove:
options: No gross neglect, misfeasance or breach of duty

traps: Applying AMT under the default regime.

viva.q: What is book profit for MAT?
viva.model: The net profit shown in the Companies Act profit and loss statement, then adjusted for the items listed in section 206.
Non-corporate assessees claiming profit-linked Chapter VIII-C or section 46 deductions whose regular tax is lower than 18.5% of adjusted total income.

viva.q: How is a member's share in an AOP taxed if the AOP paid at the maximum marginal rate?
viva.model: It is excluded from the member's total income.

viva.q: Is partial partition of a HUF recognised?
viva.model: Partial partitions are ignored for tax; the HUF continues to be assessed as before.

mcqs.explain: Total income is nil after deduction. In practice: AMT check.
Deduction added back. In practice: section 206(2).
18.5% × 2 crore. In practice: credit for future years.

mcqs.explain: Companies face MAT. In practice: 14% of book profit.
